thread:
Dave Chen: Heads up — saw an unexpected privilege elevation in the private control plane logs at 2026-03-19T13:04:23Z from an on-prem host (10.8.0.23). The action was `list_keys` against the control-plane KMS wrapper and the audit shows auth_method=role_mapping_v2 and outcome=allowed. This looks like it correlates with the RBAC refactor we shipped ~12:50 UTC (PR #4826).

Dave Chen: Relevant audit snippet:
```
2026-03-19T13:04:23Z host=control-01.prv.redwood svc=controlplane user=onprem-admin principal=group:edge-admins action=list_keys resource=controlplane auth_method=role_mapping_v2 outcome=allowed src_ip=10.8.0.23
```

Maria Gomez: Ugh. Can you paste the role-mapping entry that matched? want to see the claim conditions.

Dave Chen: Pasting the mapping we shipped in PR 4826:
```yaml
role_mappings:
  - role: privileged
    match:
      any_of:
        - claim: groups
          equals: edge-admins
        - claim: cn
          regex: ".*-edge-admins"
```

Raj Patel: KMS logs show decryption requests from the control-plane service account at the same timestamp. Could be the role mapping allowed service-account impersonation via a group claim that is forgeable on some on-prem identity providers.

Alice Nguyen: I'm pausing the RBAC rollout and rolling back PR 4826 immediately. @oncall create an incident and page SRE + sec. Also revoke the `privileged` grant for the onprem-admin role in prod as a mitigation.

oncall: PagerDuty incident created INC-7842, paging: @raj.patel @alice.nguyen @dave.chen. Assigned to eng-sre and eng-security.

Dave Chen: Scoped mitigation: added temporary network-level deny for 10.8.0.23 on the private control-plane LB and revoked the role mapping entry from the live RBAC config. Commands run:
```bash
# block host at LB
iptables -I INPUT -s 10.8.0.23 -j DROP
# remove mapping (k8s patch)
kubectl -n controlplane patch cm rbac-config --type=json -p='[{"op": "remove", "path": "/data/role_mappings/0"}]'
```

security-bot: Audit record created: SEC-INC-2026; Jira ticket SEC-382. Notifying compliance.

Maria Gomez: Starting data-access review: checking object storage/model artifact access for that principal between 2026-03-18 and now. Initial S3 access logs scanning in progress.

Raj Patel: KMS key material NOT exported. Calls were Decrypt/Describe only. No sign of key rotation or export. However we should rotate the key-encryption-envelope (KEK) and force a short-lived credential path for control-plane service account. I'll own KMS rotation/validation.

Alice Nguyen: Good. Also increment logging verbosity for role_mapping_v2 to capture the JWT claim payload that matched. We need traceable evidence of what was presented to the matcher. Add a short-lived instrumentation flag so we don't flood logs.

Dave Chen: Revert PR merged: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4879 (revert 4826). Rolling a canary revert to 10% first.

oncall: Canary revert initiated at 13:45 UTC. Monitoring set for 60m.

Maria Gomez: Data review update: found two metadata GETs for model-manifest from the controlplane service account at 13:04:27Z, no artifact downloads. No S3 object GET bytes >0 for model artifacts in that window. Will continue 24h lookback.

Raj Patel: KMS rotation scheduled, will perform envelope rotation and force reissue of control-plane session tokens. ETA 6h.

Alice Nguyen: Owners and action items:
- raj.patel: KMS audit + envelope rotation + post-rotation validation
- maria.gomez: full data access review & compliance summary for SEC-382
- dave.chen: RBAC revert verification, add unit + e2e tests for allowlist enforcement and immutable mapping checks
- alice.nguyen: postmortem + release gate to require e2e before RBAC changes go to prod

Dave Chen: Added tests branch: https://github.com/redwood/repo/compare/rbac-tests. Will open follow-up PR to add JWT claim fuzzing to prevent group-claim forgery.

security-bot: SEC-INC-2026 updated: mitigation staged. Next update due in 3h.

oncall: Canary passed (no regressions) at 14:18 UTC. Revert rolled to 100% by 14:30 UTC. Monitoring window extended to 12h.

Maria Gomez: Final note from data review after 12h: no suspicious downloads or exfil observed. Only control-plane metadata reads. Compliance notified and will expect the postmortem doc.

Alice Nguyen: Closing incident after 12h observation. Postmortem assigned to maria.gomez, target draft in 3 business days. We'll add an RBAC canary checklist to release playbooks. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
